objective: Fix exactly one remaining Phase-3 finding (F1: small-viewport horizontal overflow from an unwrapped claim-ID string), verify no regression, and close Product Demo Hardening if resolved cleanly.

NVDA Structure Graph.note: individual AlphaCard evidence-claim-id <code> elements measured wide internally (up to 680px), but proven via a direct expand-and-remeasure test NOT to affect document.scrollWidth even when their containing <details> is opened -- confirmed NOT part of F1, correctly left unmodified.

f1_reproduction_before_fix.root_cause_investigation: The global `code` CSS rule (styles.css) sets only font-family/font-size/background/padding/border-radius -- no overflow-wrap or word-break. A claim_id string ('<run_id>:<agent>:<source>:claim:<n>') contains no spaces and no default line-break opportunities under normal word-break rules, so at a narrow viewport the <code> element renders at its full intrinsic width and pushes the page wider than the viewport. The project already had an identical, narrowly-scoped precedent fix for this exact problem on .unclassified-finding-card (overflow-wrap: anywhere) -- the plain .analyst-output-card family (used by ordinary Positive/Negative findings) had never received the same treatment.

exact_root_element.component: FindingCard (frontend/src/pages/ResearchRunPage.tsx) -- the ordinary Positive/Negative Analyst findings card
exact_root_element.container_class_missing_the_fix: .analyst-output-card (shared base class for both FindingCard and UnclassifiedFindingCard; only the latter's additional .unclassified-finding-card class already had the fix)

implementation_fix.approach: Narrowest, claim-ID/metadata-value-specific styling -- NOT a global `code` element change.
implementation_fix.exact_change: Added `.analyst-output-card { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` to frontend/src/styles.css, directly adjacent to the existing, structurally identical `.unclassified-finding-card { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` rule it mirrors. Since .analyst-output-card is the shared base class for every finding card (ordinary and unclassified alike), this closes the gap for ordinary Positive/Negative findings without touching the global `code` selector, AlphaCard's evidence-claim-id, Alpha ID badges, ticker symbols, headings, buttons, or navigation.
implementation_fix.why_this_property: Allows the browser to break the string at any character only when it would otherwise overflow its container -- ordinary prose (which already has spaces to wrap at) is visually unaffected; the claim_id itself is never truncated, ellipsized, hidden, or altered, and remains fully selectable/copyable (confirmed: computed style user-select remained 'auto').
